subject: Dedicated capacity: autoscaling + integration follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Lee <john.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Dedicated capacity: autoscaling + integration follow-up

Hi John  thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) Recap of needs:
- You want dedicated capacity for predictable throughput for your customer-facing search/rerank flows.
- Primary traffic: embeddings-based semantic search + a reranker that runs on top of generated candidates.
- Target p50 latency for in-app searches: ~120200ms. Peak queries: ~1,200 qps (batched) with bursts to 2,500.
- Auth: you mentioned Okta-backed SSO for engineers + API key rotation for service calls.

2) Immediate integration/architecture items we promised to confirm:
- SDK setup & auth patterns (node/python snippets)
- Routing: how to route live vs background requests (low-latency vs batch) and fallback to hosted models
- Structured output / tool-calling constraints for the reranker stage
- Embeddings / reranker placement: whether you want embeddings precomputed or on-demand
- Autoscaling, throughput sizing, concurrency limits, and queue sizing for Dedicated capacity

3) Next steps / asks for you (so our infra sizing matches reality):
- Can you share a 2448h sample of qps by minute (CSV is fine) and typical request payload sizes (average tokens / embed dims)?
- Confirm which models you plan to use for generation versus reranker (model names + sequence lengths).
- Confirm whether you need per-tenant isolation (separate tenant pools) or a shared pool with request tagging.

4) What we'll send back by EOD tomorrow:
- Recommended Dedicated capacity config (GPU pool sizing, autoscale thresholds, concurrency targets)
- Example SDK auth snippet and sample redwood-dedicated YAML config
- Queue-sizing guidance for your burst profile

Attaching: architecture-diagram.pdf (high level call flow)  internal config sample will follow.

Would love the CSV sample and model names; once we have them Aditya will propose the GPU sizing and Dev will send the sample config. Also proposing a 301minute follow-up with your infra team on Wed (10am PT)  does that work?

Thanks,
Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Marissa  thanks for the recap, this is great. A few answers and a couple of clarifying questions: 

Answers:
- Attached is a 48h sample (acme-traffic.csv) with per-minute qps; peak minutes hit ~2,200 and typical sustained is ~9001,100.
- Payload sizes: average prompt ~450 tokens, reranker inputs ~4 candidates (generate + rerank step), embeddings are 768-d vectors precomputed for documents (we store them in Faiss).
- Models: Gen = open/llama-3-13b (we're testing), Reranker = rerank-v1 (custom model hosted via your platform eventually).
- Isolation: shared pool with request tagging should be fine to start; we may ask for tenant isolation later.

Questions:
- We use Okta webhooks + short-lived service tokens for internal services. Will that work with the Dedicated control plane or do you recommend a separate API key flow?
- For embeddings/rerank: we precompute doc embeddings, but reranker needs fresh context tokens passed in the request  does the Dedicated setup support zero-copy passing for larger contexts?

I'll confirm the Wed 10am PT time once I check with infra. Thanks again  attaching the CSV.

John

john.lee@acme.com

Thanks John  that data is perfect. A few notes based on what you sent and answers to your questions: 

Auth / keys:
- Okta shortlived tokens are fine for interactive / infra engineer flows. For service-to-service traffic into Dedicated we recommend a shortlived API key (rotated) issued by your platform and validated by our control plane; we'll provide a sample rotation webhook.

Embeddings / zero-copy:
- Dedicated supports passing large contexts; we have a zero-copy path for planned colocated inference (depends on VM/GPU sizing). We'll call out when that becomes available in the sample config.

Autoscaling & queue sizing (draft):
- Baseline: recommend reserving a pool sized for sustained qps (~1,200) and an autoscale buffer to handle +2x bursts (policy with graceful queueing).
- Concurrency: target 812 concurrent inferences per GPU for the generation model (depends on quantization); reranker can be higher concurrency if it uses fewer tokens.
- Queue sizing: keep a fast-path queue for low-latency requests (max wait 100150ms) and a background queue for batched processing  we can size the background queue to absorb ~5 minutes of peak traffic as a buffer.

Attached: redwood-dedicated-sample-config.yaml (draft) and a short snippet you can drop into your SDK.

Proposed follow-up: Wed 14 Apr 2027, 10:00 AM PT  include your infra/ops person, Dev will join to walk the config. If that works I'll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: autoscaling + integration follow-up

Adding a few technical sizing notes from infra: 

- GPU sizing: for llama-3-13b with FP16 + 4-bit quantization we see ~200250 tokens/sec per A100-equivalent for generation under our batching settings; with 450-token prompts that maps to ~0.450.55 r/s per GPU, so to reach 1,200 qps you need to rely on batching (we expect effective throughput to be much higher)  rough starting point: 812 GPUs for baseline with autoscale to 20 for burst headroom depending on batching efficiency.
- KV cache & batching: enable per-session KV caching for chat flows to reduce repeated compute; continuous batching will increase effective throughput but adds a few ms latency tail  we can tune for your 120200ms p50 target.
- Concurrency config: recommend default concurrency cap of 10 per model-worker; set per-route overrides for reranker (e.g., 20) and background batch workers (unbounded with rate limits).
- Queue formula (simple): queue_size = peak_qps * max_burst_window_seconds. For a 5minute buffer and 2,200 peak qps, queue_capacity ~= 2,200 * 300 = 660,000 (you'll use batching & sampling to avoid memory blowup). We'll discuss retention/eviction policies.

I'll paste a short SDK auth snippet in the follow-up doc and link to an internal runbook: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/DE-2391-infra-notes

Aditya
